qa_categories.label: api-interface-contract-test (+contract-test)
qa_categories.command: cmd /c moon run cmd/ed25519_kat --target native  &&  cmd /c moon run cmd/knownhosts_kat --target native -- verify_c/_knownhosts_ref_out.txt  &&  cmd /c moon run cmd/proposal_kat --target native
qa_categories.evidence: A contract test here means: MoonBit's answer must equal an INDEPENDENT implementation's answer, byte for byte. The Python/C oracles under scripts/, host/ and verify_c/ generate the .mbt vectors that cmd/*_kat replay. Probed: `moon run cmd/ed25519_kat --target native` exits 0 'ALL PASS'; `cmd/knownhosts_kat` exits 0 'ALL PASS' WHEN GIVEN ITS VECTOR FILE (without the argument it panics on a usage message and aborts 0xC0000409 -- it is a file-reading driver, not a bare KAT); `cmd/proposal_kat` exits 0. MERGED with the brief's `contract-test`: same command, same evidence. Two rows differing only in a label are the duplication this project has already been burned by.

qa_categories.label: benchmark
qa_categories.evidence: Probed, and it fails today for TWO independent reasons -- both reproduced. (1) At module scope, `moon bench --target native` exits 1 with Error [4156]: src/wt_socket/socket.mbt declares `extern "wasm"` fns, and 'import is unsupported in native backend'. (2) Per package, `moon bench cmd/bench_cached --target native` exits 0 while printing 'Total tests: 0, passed: 0, failed: 0' and 'Warning: no test entry found.' The repo contains zero *_bench.mbt files (the only hits under .mooncakes/ are vendored dependencies). Reason (2) is why ci.py gained an opt-in zero-work guard: without it this row would have reported a PASS having measured nothing. The real benchmark numbers come from cmd/bench_* run as native .exe -- see the performance-test row.

qa_categories.label: e2e-test
qa_categories.evidence: Real gates, excluded from the default tier because they need a live SSH peer and/or a browser Worker. cmd/wt_ssh's own header: 'result: ESTABLISHED' means a real OpenSSH server accepted the handshake inside a browser Worker. ci/ci.py keeps the MEASURED exclusion list (PEER_GATES = verify_loop31..39) rather than a keyword scan, because loop53 mentions playwright yet runs in seconds.

qa_categories.label: format-check
qa_categories.evidence: Probed: `moon fmt --check` exists and exits -1 today. It wants to re-wrap the KAT byte arrays in cmd/aes_test/main.mbt and add a trailing newline. Run with --check ONLY: AGENTS.md records that `moon fmt` in write mode corrupts CJK comments (真实加密 -> 真加密).

qa_categories.label: fuzz-test
qa_categories.evidence: No fuzzer exists in the toolchain (`moon --help` has none), but cmd/sftp_fault IS fault injection and was classified by reading main.mbt: its own header says it pushes malformed packets through `chan_step`/`ChanState`, re-slicing the vectors at 5 cut points to prove the state machine. Probed: exit 0, 'ALL PASS (50/50 runs, 10 scenarios x 5 cut points)'. Deterministic vectors, not random generation -- honest name is fault-injection fuzzing.

qa_categories.label: gherkin-test
qa_categories.evidence: PROBE CONTRADICTS THE BRIEF, and the probe wins. `moon search gherkin` exits 0 and finds moonrockz/gherkin@0.5.1 (a Gherkin parser with DOM/visitor/fold/SAX APIs); `moon search cucumber` finds moonrockz/cucumber-expressions@0.6.1. So the ecosystem DOES exist. It is not_available FOR THIS REPOSITORY, not for MoonBit: neither package is declared in moon.mod, the repo contains zero *.feature / *.feature.md files, and adding a third-party dependency is forbidden by the task's own constraints.

qa_categories.evidence: These drive several src packages together through a real protocol conversation rather than one package's unit tests. Probed: `moon run cmd/kexdh_test --target native` exit 0 'dh14_consistency: MATCH'; cmd/channel_test exit 0 'chan_io_coverage: PASS'; cmd/sftp_test exit 0 'ALL PASS (24 session cases, 7 inbuf cases)'; cmd/userauth_test exit 0. They need no SSH peer -- the peer-shaped ones are the e2e-test row.

qa_categories.label: load-stress-test
qa_categories.evidence: Classified from the code, not the directory names. Read cmd/sftp_fault, cmd/sftp_mitm, cmd/sftp_test, cmd/wt_ssh and cmd/wt_net: sftp_fault drives 10 malformed scenarios x 5 cut points through ChanState -- that is fault injection into parsers (see fuzz-test), not load. cmd/wt_* need a browser Worker. cmd/probe_async_wall is a setTimeout race probe, not a load driver. A repo-wide grep for load|stress|soak|throughput|rps|concurren|flood matched 4 files, none of them a load harness. No concurrent session generator, no rate driver, no soak test exists.

qa_categories.label: mutation-test
qa_categories.evidence: host/loop*_mutations.py: 20 harnesses that edit the working tree, run `moon clean`, re-run the gate that owns the decision, and restore. Owned by the mutations tier and NOT in the qa tier on purpose: each one is many full gate runs and they mutate the tree, so they must never run concurrently with anything else here. Invoke with `python ci/ci.py --tiers mutations`.

qa_categories.label: performance-test
qa_categories.evidence: Probed: `node host/bench_modpow.mjs` builds cmd/bench_slow, bench_fast and bench_cached in release and times 50 x 2048-bit modexp per program by running the native .exe directly, so the number is compute cost and not toolchain startup. Exit 0, and the three implementations agree byte-exact on the same value. This is the comparative regression signal; the `benchmark` row is the toolchain's own facility.

qa_categories.label: security-scan-dast
qa_categories.evidence: PROBE CONTRADICTS THE BRIEF, and the probe wins. The brief listed DAST as simply absent; the real blocker is sharper. No DAST tool for MoonBit exists, AND DAST requires a running deployment to aim at -- this repository ships a client library, not a service. `moon --help` on 0.1.20261012 offers no security/scanner subcommand of any kind. The peer-gates tier (e2e-test) is as close as this project gets, because those gates drive a real OpenSSH server.

qa_categories.label: security-scan-sast
qa_categories.command: cmd /c node host\verify_loop60.mjs  &&  cmd /c node host\verify_loop61.mjs
qa_categories.evidence: No SAST product exists for MoonBit. The closest real thing is targeted at the vulnerability class this project actually hit: 'declared runnable != actually runnable'. Loop #59 shipped a proposal naming hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com, which src/bpacket cannot run, and nothing failed for loops. src/bpacket/runnable.mbt (Loop #60) and src/kexflow/runnable.mbt (Loop #61) enforce the allow-lists, and verify_loop60/61.mjs assert them. Probed: `node host/verify_loop60.mjs` exit 0 '78/78 checks passed', `node host/verify_loop61.mjs` exit 0 '62/62 checks passed'. Deliberately NOT the same command as the static-analysis row -- this is a domain-specific rule, not a compiler diagnostic.
